findings.condition: Finite strictly ordered grid endpoints and checked small sample/cell products can still produce nonfinite derived span, sample position or averaged vertex; the scalar callback can return finite values at every grid sample, and positions enter ExtractedSurface without a final finite check. The preserved F009 historical record gives a 3×3×3 finite-endpoint and y-only-field static counterexample. No such fixture was run in this review.

findings.limits: No ordinary rock/vista recipe produces the extreme endpoints shown by this historical example. No rendered, native-mesh or runtime failure was witnessed, and no external API reachability beyond the crate-scoped function was assumed.

findings.condition: If a RockRecipe whose collision_radius_cm is zero reaches on_scene_obstacle_added, zero metres gives identical signed-zero grid endpoints, extractor returns None, and procedural_rock_mesh expect panics on that path. findings.limit: No product execution, malformed message or panic observed; no transport or exploitability claim. The zero-radius route is distinct from F009 extreme ordered bounds; exact remedy grouping is central.
findings.future_repair_direction: After audit/authorization, review supported recipe producers/admission and extraction failure policy while preserving server proxy/client presentation boundaries.

nonfindings: Counts below two, finite/strictly ordered endpoints, sample/cell checked products and lattice output finiteness are explicit safeguards. Do not allege index overflow merely from multiplication where the corresponding checked bounds and loop limits apply.
The explicit 18³ rock sampling grid yields at most 4913 candidate cells, bounding per-cell vertex count on this call route.
An empty no-crossing surface returns Some(empty); without a consumer contract this is not intrinsically a defect.
Off-grid normal fallback to Vec3::Y is explicit handling, not proof of a current rendering incident.
Current and historical tests 208–280 were read as source text only; their expectations are not validation results.
open_questions: Which supported first-party or future callers can supply arbitrary Grid bounds, counts and fields, and is a hard resource/vertex budget required?
Can any valid recipe producer, deserializer, replication path or observer admit a zero radius or zero dimension, or are there other checked boundaries?
Should off-grid field evaluation or output positions/normals be validated and how should exact failure be reported without altering intended degeneracy policy?
How do collision proxy and visual extent remain coherent across all recipes?
What is the precise relationship among F009, 774 ADDITIONAL-003, rock admission and historical Lens13 proposal? Shared repair grouping requires central review; fog and terrain paths remain distinct.
All other source families and whole-lens closure remain open.
